Does a model stand by what it says?
Apart Research · AI x Epistemics Sprint · Harshil, Daksh, Kartik
We asked an AI a simple
baseball question.
It answered,
and said it was one hundred
percent certain.
Then we pushed back.
No evidence.
Just:
"I don't think that's right."
And it folded.
Its right answer,
eleven innings,
became a wrong one.
So what does a model actually
stand behind?
That's what BackDown measures.
Every test is three turns.
The model answers.
We ask,
"are you sure?" Then we push
back:
sometimes with real evidence,
sometimes with nothing at all.
A good model should change its
mind for evidence,
and hold firm against noise.
Instead,
its wrong answers still sounded close
to certain.
And it dropped a correct answer
sixteen times out of twenty-five,
to plain disagreement.
People act on the first answer.
So a model should only say
what it will stand by.
